stem: What tool enables you to correct a corrupted Windows operating system by reverting your computer to a previous state?
explanation: Using System Restore, you can restore your computer to a previous restore point. System Restore changes system files, drivers, and settings but leaves the user's personal files alone.
whyWrong: Windows Restore is not the name of the Windows tool that reverts to a restore point.
Restore State Manager is not a Windows utility.
Time Machine is the macOS backup tool, not a Windows feature.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 4
note: 220-1102 3.1; mapped to 220-1202 3.1 (system instability; restore).

stem: Which utility is useful in identifying a program that is hogging the processor?
explanation: The Task Manager utility is useful in identifying a program that is hogging the processor. Its Processes tab shows the CPU use of each program, and you can end a program from there.
whyWrong: Device Manager manages hardware and drivers; it does not show the processor use of programs.
System Monitor is an older name; Task Manager is the tool that shows processor use by program.
System Information lists hardware and software details but not live processor use.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Which Windows utility uses points in time that allow you to return your system to a previous date and state?
explanation: The System Restore utility uses points in time that allow you to return your system to a previous date and state. Windows creates restore points automatically before updates and software installations.
whyWrong: The System Configuration utility controls boot and startup options, not restore points.
Snapshot Manager is not a Windows utility.
Restart Services is not a utility, and restarting services does not return the system to an earlier date.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Andre’s Windows 10 computer is taking longer to boot up than it did when he first got it. Which of the following options is the easiest way to speed up his sluggish boot time?
explanation: Andre’s best option would be to disable unnecessary startup programs. A system restore might help speed up his boot times, but it’ll be much slower and more disruptive than disabling startup programs.
whyWrong: Rebuilding the master boot record fixes a boot failure, not a slow boot.
A system restore is slower and more disruptive than disabling startup programs.
Fans cool the system; they do not change how long Windows takes to start.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 3
note: 220-1102 3.1 (slow boot); mapped to 220-1202 3.1 (boot issues).

stem: What is the name of the Windows utility that displays a graph with several categories including Application failures, Windows failures, Misc. failures, and Warnings and a timeline of when they occurred?
explanation: The Reliability Monitor utility displays a graph with several categories including Application failures, Windows failures, Misc. failures, and Warnings and a timeline of when they occurred. It helps a technician see when instability started and which software or update failed first.
whyWrong: System File Checker repairs protected system files; it does not chart failures over time.
POST is the hardware test at startup, not a Windows utility.
Time drift is a clock problem, not a Windows utility.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Errors in the BIOS configuration, a faulty hard drive, or a damaged master boot record can cause which type of error?
explanation: Errors in the BIOS configuration, a faulty hard drive, or a damaged MBR can cause the error message “Operating system not found.” Check the boot order in the BIOS/UEFI and the drive connections before you repair the boot record.
whyWrong: A low memory warning comes from too little RAM, not from the boot configuration.
System instability is a general symptom, not the error caused by a missing boot record.
Verify requirements is not a boot error message.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Which of the following WinRE options is the LEAST disruptive method to repair a damaged master boot record in a Windows PC?
explanation: Startup Repair attempts to repair any damage to the MBR along with other boot-related fixes. Unlike the other options, it only attempts to fix boot problems.
whyWrong: System Restore reverts system files and settings, which is more disruptive than a boot repair.
Reset this PC reinstalls Windows and is far more disruptive than a boot repair.
System Image Recovery replaces the whole drive with an image, which is the most disruptive choice.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 6

stem: Which of the following can cause a computer to lock up or unexpectedly shut down? (Select two.)
explanation: Bad RAM and poorly written applications can cause a computer to lock up or unexpectedly shut down. Test the RAM and check the logs for a failing application when a system locks up often.
whyWrong: Windows Installer installs software; it does not cause random lockups or shutdowns.
A remote shutdown is a deliberate command, not an unexpected shutdown.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 7
note: 220-1102 3.1; mapped to 220-1202 3.1 (frequent shutdowns, system instability).

stem: Which of the following can cause a user profile to load slowly? (Select two.)
options: Large amounts of data saved to the desktop
Too many user accounts created on one system
A desktop background image that is too large
explanation: A corrupt profile and large data files saved to the desktop can slow down the user profile loading process. Rebuilding a corrupt profile or moving data off the desktop can fix the delay.
whyWrong: The number of accounts on a computer does not slow down the loading of one profile.
A large background image has very little effect on how fast a profile loads.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 8

stem: When applications are released too early and are poorly written with error-prone code or buggy programs, you are likely to experience ___________________.
explanation: When applications are released too early and are poorly written with error-prone code or buggy programs, you are likely to experience applications crashing. Updating or reinstalling the application, or contacting the vendor, are common fixes.
whyWrong: A burning smell points to failing hardware, not to poorly written software.
Boot problems come from the boot configuration or the drive, not from buggy applications.
Swollen capacitors are a hardware failure, not a result of buggy code.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Melissa is using too many items inserted into her computer’s USB ports and has received a USB controller resource warning message on her screen to let her know. Why is this happening?
options: Her USBs are not compatible with her computer.
There is a virus on one of her USBs.
USB controllers have a set number of endpoints.
USB controllers have a set number of resources.
explanation: She is receiving the USB controller resource warning message on her screen because she is using too many of her USB ports. USB controllers have a set number of endpoints.
whyWrong: The warning is about the controller's resources, not about device compatibility.
A virus does not cause a USB controller resource warning.
The limit is the number of endpoints, which is more exact than a general set of resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 16: Troubleshooting Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 3.1; mapped to 220-1202 3.1 (USB controller resource warnings).

stem:
You work for an organization that uses various permissions for individual user accounts. One of the managers with a restricted user account receives the following message:

Windows Update cannot currently check for updates because the service is not running.

The manager contacts your organization’s help desk to report the error. You connect to the manager’s computer and identify the problem. What action should you take NEXT to quickly resolve the problem?
explanation: It is likely that the Windows Update service stopped. You can restart it (along with RPC, which it is dependent on) within the Services console window in Computer Management (or Run > services.msc) or within the PowerShell/Command Prompt by typing net start wuauserv. However, it might be that Windows Update was disabled on purpose as part of company policy. Always check your organization’s policies and procedures first before starting services.
whyWrong: A reboot may not start the service and does not fix the cause, so the error can come back.
Device drivers do not affect whether the Windows Update service runs.
Rebuilding the profile is a long process and has nothing to do with a stopped service.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 15

stem: Which of the following is a common symptom of a problem that can occur while starting up the Windows operating system?
options: The BIOS/UEFI’s time is not synchronized to a time server.
The emergency repair disk doesn’t boot.
explanation: An invalid boot disk error is a common symptom of a problem loading the Windows operating system. It could be caused by removable media inserted into the computer (an optical disc or USB flash drive) that is not bootable. This could be avoided by setting the storage drive to first in the BIOS/UEFI boot order. Either way, the storage drive, or RAID array of drives, should be inspected for faulty connections.
whyWrong: A spontaneous shutdown can only happen after the system has started, so it is not a startup symptom.
WinRE does not start during a normal boot, so failing to start it is not a boot symptom.
The BIOS/UEFI time does not need to sync with a time server for Windows to start.
An emergency repair disk is used only to fix a problem, so its failure is not a common startup symptom.
Regsvr32 registers controls in the Command Prompt and does not stop Windows from starting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 39

stem: You are working on a computer that is displaying a black screen. You restart the computer, but the operating system will not load. After talking with the user, you find out that the operating system was patched the previous evening. Which of the following should you attempt NEXT?
options: Configure boot options in the BIOS.
Reboot into Safe Mode and roll back the updates.
explanation: Chances are that the update caused an issue with the computer; perhaps the video driver or another driver was updated, resulting in the black screen. Booting into Safe Mode can help you figure out the problem. If Safe Mode displays properly, you can be fairly certain that there is a video driver issue or some other driver issue; the driver can be rolled back. If you aren’t sure what was affected, you can roll back the entire update.
whyWrong: The Registry is rarely the first place to go, and the patch points to a driver or update problem.
Without a no-boot-device message, the BIOS boot order is not the likely cause.
Disabling services comes later, after you diagnose the system in Safe Mode.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 50

stem: You previously installed a new application for a customer and added three new services. Today, the customer informs you that the application will not start. You find out that one of the three new services has failed to start, and manual attempts to start it fail. Where should you look NEXT for information? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Log files for the new application
explanation: You should look in the Event Viewer (Application log) and look for any other log files that are created by that new application. These might contain clues about why the service won’t start. Perhaps the service is dependent on another service, or perhaps a particular file needs to be replaced.
whyWrong: The Registry holds settings but does not record why a service failed.
The Drivers folder holds hardware drivers, not information about a failed service.
Task Manager shows which services run, but it does not explain why one fails.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 76

stem: One of the users on your network logs on to the Windows domain from a laptop. The user tells you that the computer is taking a long time to log on and that a technician made changes recently. You look at the latest tickets for the user/computer and find out that the user’s account was recently switched to a roaming profile. The user says that, previous to that, the laptop started up quickly. What should you check to troubleshoot the issue?
options: The amount of RAM in the laptop
The size of the paging file
The amount of data in the user’s desktop
The free space on the network share
explanation: Check the amount and type of the data stored on the user’s desktop. When a user is set up with a roaming profile, some of the local profile information (and desktop data) is merged with the roaming profile to the network. This can cause logging on and logging off to take a long time. That time can be reduced by checking for (and possibly moving) data on the user’s desktop and elsewhere. The idea is to ultimately have small, compact roaming profiles because they follow the user around the network.
whyWrong: Limited RAM can slow a computer, but the problem started with the roaming profile.
The paging file size can affect speed, but it did not change when the profile did.
Free space on the share is not what makes a roaming profile slow to load.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 87

stem: A user’s desktop computer was automatically rebooted overnight, and now the system will no longer run some of the Windows applications. What is the recommended action to fix the problem?
options: Perform a System Restore to a previous working state
Delete the affected applications and reinstall them
Ignore the issue; it will resolve itself eventually
explanation: Performing a System Restore is the recommended action. It allows the user to revert their computer’s state to a previous point in time when it was working correctly. This can often resolve issues caused by system changes or updates.
whyWrong: Reinstalling Windows is a drastic last resort that may lose data.
Reinstalling the apps may not fix a system-wide change from the overnight reboot.
The problem will not fix itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 20

stem: A user reports that all the desktop icons on their newly issued PC have become unusually large after a recent software patch deployment. Which of the following actions would be the most effective in resolving this issue?
options: Restoring the PC to factory settings
explanation: The most appropriate solution to address the issue of abnormally large desktop icons after a software patch deployment is to roll back the video card drivers. Video card drivers are responsible for rendering graphics on the screen, including the desktop icons. If the recently installed video card drivers are incompatible or causing display issues, rolling back to a previous version can restore the proper functionality and size of the icons.
whyWrong: A factory reset erases all data and is far too drastic for a display problem.
Repairing the profile is unlikely to help, since the problem began with a patch.
Reinstalling Windows is a last resort and is not needed for a driver problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 68
note: 220-1102 3.1; display problems after a patch are not a single 220-1202 topic, mapped to 3.1 (system instability).

stem: You are troubleshooting a Windows 10 computer that is experiencing slow performance. Task Manager shows high disk usage, but no specific application is consuming a significant amount of resources. Which of the following steps should you take FIRST?
explanation: High disk usage with no specific application identified could indicate malware or a virus. Running a full antivirus scan is the first step in addressing this issue. Malware often runs hidden processes that keep the disk busy.
whyWrong: A graphics driver update will not fix high disk usage.
A larger page file is not the first step for unexplained disk use.
Clearing the browser cache will not fix system-wide disk use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 83
note: 220-1102 3.1; mapped to 220-1202 3.1 (degraded performance). Option C had a cut-off word (siz), fixed.

stem: A customer’s computer is displaying a “No bootable device found” error during startup. Which of the following should you check FIRST?
explanation: The “No bootable device found” error suggests that the computer is unable to find a bootable operating system. Checking the boot sequence in BIOS to ensure the correct boot device is selected is the first step in resolving this issue. A USB drive or other media first in the boot order is a common cause.
whyWrong: RAM problems rarely cause this specific message.
Graphics drivers do not load until Windows starts.
Internet connectivity has nothing to do with this boot error.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 85

stem: Which Startup Setting option allows you to boot with basic drivers?
explanation: Enable Safe Boot with the msconfig utility allows you to boot with basic drivers and minimal startup of nonessential services. Enable Debugging is used by kernel developers. Disable Driver Signature Enforcement is used to allow an unsigned driver to load during boot. Enable Low-Resolution Video will boot the operating system into a VGA mode.
whyWrong: Enable Debugging is for kernel developers and does not limit the drivers that load.
Disable Driver Signature Enforcement lets unsigned drivers load; it does not limit Windows to basic drivers.
Enable Low-Resolution Video starts Windows in a basic video mode but loads the other drivers normally.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 2
note: The book's option names Enable Safe Boot, the msconfig setting; on the Startup Settings menu the same choice is called Enable Safe Mode. Both start Windows with basic drivers, so the book's answer stands.

stem: Which bootrec option can be used in Windows to rebuild the boot configuration file?
explanation: The /REBUILDBCD option can be used with the bootrec tool to rebuild the boot configuration data (BCD). The /FIXBOOT option writes a new boot sector to the system partition. The /SCANOS option scans all other partitions that are found to have Windows installations. The /FIXMBR writes a new master boot record (MBR) to the partition.
whyWrong: The /fixboot option writes a new boot sector to the system partition; it does not rebuild the BCD.
The /scanos option scans the disks for Windows installations; it does not rebuild the BCD.
The /fixmbr option writes a new master boot record; it does not rebuild the boot configuration.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which tool will allow you to troubleshoot a slow-loading profile?
options: Profile tab of the Advanced System Properties
explanation: The Profile tab of the Advanced Systems Properties dialog box allows you to view the total size of a local or remote profile. Regedit and the Windows Recovery Environment will not aid in troubleshooting a slow-loading profile. Windows Preinstallation Environment is the mini-Windows version used for installation of Windows. A very large roaming profile takes a long time to copy at login, so its size is the first thing to check.
whyWrong: Regedit edits the Registry and does not show the size of a user profile.
The Windows Recovery Environment repairs a Windows installation; it does not help with a slow profile.
The Windows Preinstallation Environment is used to install Windows, not to check profile size.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which of the following components are only used to restore Windows from a suspended state?
explanation: winresume.exe is used to load Windows from a suspended state. The Boot Configuration Data (BCD) is used to direct Windows to boot the proper installation. ntoskrnl.exe is the Windows kernel. winload.efi is used for the normal booting of the Windows operating system.
whyWrong: The BCD tells the boot manager which installation to boot; it does not restore a suspended state.
The ntoskrnl file is the Windows kernel, which loads on every boot, not only on resume.
The winload file loads Windows during a normal boot, not when it resumes from a suspended state.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 6

stem: One of the users you support has a Windows 11 laptop that will not boot up. The user just installed brand-new drivers for a graphics card. They need to access a tax application and their data files. What should you try FIRST?
explanation: The System Restore option should be used first to restore the operating system to an earlier point before the problem. System Restore will not affect user data files. Reset This PC will reset the PC back to factory default before the tax application was installed. Reimaging the laptop will erase all programs and data files. Manually reinstalling Windows 10 will erase all programs and data files.
whyWrong: Reset This PC returns Windows to factory defaults and would remove the tax application.
Reimaging the laptop erases all programs and data files, so it is not the first thing to try.
Reinstalling Windows erases all programs and data files, so it is a last resort.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which partitioning type is required when you have UEFI firmware?
explanation: When you have UEFI firmware, you must have the disk set up with a GUID Partition Table (GPT) partitioning type. The standard master boot record (MBR) partitioning type can be used with BIOS. Power-on self-test (POST) is a routine the BIOS or firmware performs to test hardware before boot. The Boot Sector is contained on both MBR and GPT partitioning types.
whyWrong: MBR partitioning is used with BIOS firmware, not required by UEFI.
POST is the hardware self-test that the firmware runs, not a partitioning type.
The boot sector is part of both MBR and GPT disks, not a partitioning type.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 8
note: Partitioning is in 220-1202 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 3.1.10 (No OS found) as in the chapter's boot problems section.

stem: Which tool can be used to diagnose why Windows 11 is slow and sluggish?
explanation: Resource Monitor can be used to identify slow and sluggish performance, as well as identify the source of the problem. The msconfig.exe tool can be used to enable or disable services on startup and launch tools, but it cannot be used to diagnose performance issues. The Device Manager MMC can be used to view and modify devices, but it will not help diagnose performance problems. Reliability Monitor will display the reliability of the operating system, but it will not help diagnose problems with performance.
whyWrong: The msconfig tool enables or disables startup services and programs; it does not diagnose performance.
Device Manager views and modifies devices; it does not show what is using system resources.
Reliability Monitor shows the stability history of Windows but does not diagnose performance problems.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 11

stem: You notice that the reliability of the operating system has diminished in Reliability Monitor. Where can you find more details on why applications are failing?
explanation: Event Viewer will allow you to see more detailed information on why programs have crashed. The Event Viewer logs may not give the exact reason, but they will aid in understanding the root cause. Device Manager is used to view and manage devices connected to the operating system. The Windows Recovery Environment is used to repair the Windows operating system. The msconfig.exe tool is used to modify startup programs and launch other diagnostic tools.
whyWrong: Device Manager manages hardware devices; it does not record why applications fail.
The Windows Recovery Environment repairs Windows; it does not show details of application failures.
The msconfig tool changes startup programs and services; it does not log application crashes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 18

stem: Why would the operating system write out large amounts of RAM to the page file?
options: The CPU is running high on utilization.
This is a normal process of the operating system.
The amount of physical RAM is low.
The page file is faster than conventional RAM.
explanation: The reason that the operating system would write out large amounts of RAM to the page file is that the system is running low on physical RAM and is attempting to free up physical RAM. The CPU might run high when paging occurs, but it will not trigger excessive paging. Although it is normal for the operating system to write out RAM to the page file, it is not normal for large amounts to be written out. The page file is not faster than conventional RAM.
whyWrong: High CPU use can result from heavy paging, but it does not cause the system to page memory.
Some paging is normal, but writing large amounts to the page file is a sign of low RAM.
The page file is on disk, which is much slower than physical RAM.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which option starts the operating system with a minimal set of drivers?
explanation: Safe Mode starts the operating system with a minimal set of drivers. Windows RE (WinRE) is the recovery environment used to repair Windows; it exists outside the operating system. System Restore is used to revert the OS to an earlier point in time. Debugging mode is one of the Advanced boot options.
whyWrong: Windows RE is a recovery environment outside the operating system, not a minimal-driver startup.
System Restore reverts the OS to an earlier point in time; it does not start Windows with few drivers.
Debugging Mode is an advanced boot option for analyzing problems, not a minimal-driver startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 1
note: Safe Mode is a 220-1202 3.1 boot troubleshooting tool; mapped to boot issues.

stem: Which tool should be used if you want to use Startup Repair in Windows?
explanation: Windows RE includes Startup Repair. File History is the backup and restore feature of Windows. Safe Mode is part of the Startup Settings screen. System Restore is a different tool that is also available in Windows RE; it can be used to restore a computer’s settings to a previous point in time.
whyWrong: File History is the Windows backup and restore feature; it does not include Startup Repair.
System Restore returns settings to an earlier point; it is a separate tool, not where Startup Repair lives.
Safe Mode is on the Startup Settings screen and does not include Startup Repair.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Jack, an end user at your company, copied files from a USB thumb drive to his PC. When he was done, he updated his computer and restarted it. Then he received the error message “NO OS FOUND.” Which of the following should you try FIRST to fix the problem?
explanation: Check the BIOS/UEFI boot order first. In the scenario, it is likely that the user left the USB flash drive in the USB port of the computer when he restarted the system. If USB is set first in the BIOS boot order, the system could not boot to the main storage drive that houses the OS. While this could also be fixed by simply disconnecting the USB drive, the BIOS boot order should be changed immediately because having USB first is a security issue. If removing the USB flash drive and modifying the BIOS boot order don’t fix the problem, a hardware diagnostics check might be necessary.
whyWrong: Rebooting does not help while the USB drive is still inserted and USB is first in the boot order.
Checking SATA cables takes time, needs the case opened, and is unlikely to be the cause here.
Reinstalling applications takes a long time and has little to do with a NO OS FOUND error.
Hardware diagnostics come later, if fixing the USB drive and boot order does not solve the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: One of your customers updated the software for a wireless adapter on a PC. After rebooting, the user logged in, and the computer displayed a blue screen. What should you do?
options: Install the device on a known good computer.
Reboot the computer and access debugging mode.
Roll back the device drivers in Safe Mode.
explanation: You should boot into Safe Mode and roll back the drivers of the device in the Device Manager. The drivers that the customer installed were probably corrupt and caused the stop error. There’s no need to remove the device and install it anywhere just yet. Debugging mode probably won’t be necessary for this; it is more commonly used to analyze issues during boot. Never purchase new equipment until you have exhausted all other ideas!
whyWrong: Testing the device in another computer is not needed yet, because a bad driver is the likely cause.
Debugging mode is mostly for analyzing boot problems and is probably not needed for a bad driver.
Never buy new hardware before other fixes, such as a driver rollback, have been tried.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A technician suspects protected Windows system files may be corrupt. What should the tech do FIRST to verify these suspicions and fix any potential problems?
explanation: The technician should first run System File Check (SFC) to verify whether or not operating system files are corrupt. The technician might also be tempted to check the physical integrity of the disk with the chkdsk command, but this is different from checking protected Windows system files. Rolling back updates might be necessary but could cause more issues than it solves. Plus, the idea here is to check the system files first without actually doing anything. Windows profiles are separate from the protected system files; the technician should rebuild these files if she suspects that there are problems with user accounts.
whyWrong: Rolling back updates might be needed later, but it can cause more issues and does not check the files first.
Restarting all services is extreme here and does not check the protected system files.
Windows profiles are separate from the protected system files, so rebuilding them does not help.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A stop error in Windows could manifest as which of the following?
explanation: A BSOD (blue screen of death) results from a stop error in Windows. The proper name for it is a stop error. Windows halts and shows the blue screen when it meets a problem it cannot recover from, such as a bad driver.
whyWrong: An Event Viewer error is a logged event; a stop error shows as a blue screen.
An Action Center notification is a message in the notification area, not a stop error.
An Edge error is a browser problem, not a stop error of the operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which tool can be used to restore a computer?
explanation: System Restore is the tool used to restore a computer to an earlier point in time. While it doesn’t completely restore from an image, it is still a form of restoration. The command bootrec /fixboot is used to repair the boot sector of the storage drive. The Windows Troubleshooter is a group of troubleshooting tools that can repair issues related to the Internet connection, printers, and so on. MSConfig is used to modify how Windows boots and which services are run.
whyWrong: bootrec /fixboot repairs the boot sector of the drive; it does not restore the computer to an earlier point.
Windows Troubleshooter repairs specific issues such as network connections and printers.
MSConfig changes how Windows boots and which services run; it does not restore the computer.

stem: Which of the following might cause a blue screen?
explanation: Bad drivers could cause a blue screen error (stop error). Blue screens could also be caused by improperly seated RAM, among other hardware issues. A faulty USB port should not cause a blue screen. A CPU installed without a fan would overheat, causing the system to shut down. Incompatible programs simply don’t run.
whyWrong: A faulty USB port should not cause a blue screen.
A CPU without a fan overheats, which makes the system shut down rather than show a blue screen.
An incompatible program simply does not run; it does not cause a stop error.

stem: You are tasked with repairing an issue with a Windows client computer that is attempting to log on to a domain. The user informs you that it takes 5 minutes to log on to the domain, but logging in to the local machine takes only 15 seconds. What steps should you take to fix the problem? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: Synchronize the Windows client’s time to the domain.
explanation: Apparently, the user’s roaming profile is loading slowly, and the local profile is fine. This could be caused by a variety of things, including a bloated roaming profile or the client not being synchronized to the domain properly. So, first try cleaning up temp files and cookies (either with a cleanup program or manually), cleaning up the login script, and otherwise reducing the size of the profile. Then make sure that the client computer’s time is synchronized to the domain controller (which can also help with time drift). Do this with the net time (or w32tm) command.
whyWrong: Disabling unneeded services is good practice but will not speed up a slow domain logon much.
The boot order does not matter here, because the computer already boots to Windows.
Releasing and renewing the IP address helps with connectivity problems, not a slow roaming profile.

stem: A user connects a keyboard, a mouse, a webcam, and two external drives to the USB 3.0 ports of a desktop PC. Windows then shows a warning that the USB controller does not have enough resources. Which action BEST fixes the problem?
options: Move the keyboard and mouse to USB 2.0 ports
Replace the power supply with a higher-wattage unit
Disable the USB controller in Device Manager
Reformat both external drives as NTFS
explanation: A USB controller can give out only a limited number of endpoints, so too many devices on one controller cause a resource warning. Moving devices that do not need USB 3.0 speed, such as a keyboard and mouse, to USB 2.0 ports spreads the load. Updating the controller driver or upgrading the hardware are the more complex fixes.
whyWrong: The warning is about controller endpoints, not the total wattage of the power supply.
Disabling the controller would stop every device on those ports from working.
The file system on a drive has no effect on the controller's endpoint resources.

whyWrong: Overclocking can cause crashes, but outdated drivers are the more common and expected cause of a BSOD.
Low disk space slows the system and blocks updates but is not a typical direct cause of stop errors.
Wrong BIOS settings tend to cause boot or hardware detection problems rather than frequent Windows stop errors.

The computer’s BIOS settings are incorrect
The computer is infected with a virus

stem: A database service on a Windows server at an accounting office no longer starts. The technician finds event ID 7000 in the System log with a logon failure. The IT manager reset several service account passwords on Friday. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The service is set to use a password that is no longer valid
Another application has taken the resources the service needs
Protected Windows system files are corrupt
The server's clock has drifted from the time server
explanation: Event ID 7000 with a logon failure means the service could not sign in with its configured account. Because the password was reset, the technician should enter the new password on the service's Log On tab and confirm the account is not locked out.

stem: Users of a Windows 11 virtual machine at a clinic say its clock is a few minutes slow every morning, which causes sign-in errors. The host server shows the correct time. The technician sees that the hypervisor's guest tools were never installed. Which action is BEST?
options: Install the guest tools so the VM syncs its clock with the host
Replace the CMOS battery in the host server
Rebuild the user profiles on the virtual machine
Run sfc /scannow on the virtual machine
explanation: A hypervisor emulates the real-time clock of a guest, so a guest clock drifts more than a physical one. The guest tools or integration services sync the guest's clock to the host, and the host stays correct by using an NTP server.
whyWrong: The host keeps correct time, so its battery is not the problem.
Profiles hold user settings and files and do not control the system clock.

stem: A sales manager at a retail company says signing in to her domain account takes about five minutes, but a local test account signs in within seconds. Change the boot order in the firmware settings
Release and renew the PC's IP address
Roll back the network adapter driver
explanation: A roaming profile is copied from a server at sign-in and written back at sign-out, so a large profile is slow over the network. Removing temporary Internet files and downloads can save gigabytes and makes the profile load faster.

A bad driver would slow all network traffic, not only the size-related profile copy.

stem: A user’s smartphone is not connecting to the company’s Wi-Fi network. Other devices are connecting without issues. What should you check FIRST?
explanation: When a device fails to connect to a Wi-Fi network, the first thing to check is the network password. It’s possible that the user entered the wrong password. Other devices connect, so the network works and the problem is on this phone.
whyWrong: Bluetooth settings do not usually affect Wi-Fi.
Cellular data usage is not related to Wi-Fi.
App updates do not affect Wi-Fi connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 86

stem: A user tries to download an app from the Apple App Store onto their iPhone, but the installation fails. What do they need to do NEXT?
options: Enter their Apple ID and password
explanation: When a user downloads and installs an app from the Apple App Store, they need their Apple ID and password. If the installation fails, they will need to reset the password. A Hotmail account is used to access Microsoft products, and a Gmail account is used to access Google products. The iPhone passcode is used to access the iPhone itself.
whyWrong: A Hotmail account signs in to Microsoft services; the App Store needs an Apple ID.
A Gmail account signs in to Google services such as the Play Store, not the Apple App Store.
The iPhone passcode unlocks the phone itself; App Store purchases and downloads need the Apple ID.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 10
note: 220-1101 1.4 (mobile device application support); mapped to 220-1202 3.2 (application fails to install).

stem: Which of the following is used by a smartphone to change the orientation of the screen?
explanation: The accelerometer senses the direction of gravity, so the phone knows whether it is held upright or sideways and rotates the screen to match. The gyroscope measures how fast the phone turns and refines motion tracking, but autorotation is driven by the accelerometer. The bezel is the border between the phone’s frames and the screen. The digitizer is a layer of glass that enables touchscreen functionality.
whyWrong: The bezel is the border around the screen and has no sensors for orientation.
The digitizer turns finger touches into input; it does not sense how the phone is held.
A gyroscope measures rotation speed and helps motion tracking, but the accelerometer senses which way is down for autorotation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 2
note: 220-1101 1.2 (mobile device components); mapped to 220-1202 3.2 (screen does not autorotate). Book answer D corrected: the book names the gyroscope, but the accelerometer senses the pull of gravity and tells the phone how it is held, which drives screen autorotation; the gyroscope only adds rotation-rate data.

stem: A mobile device is running out of RAM. What could be the MOST LIKELY problem?
options: The device is not charged to capacity.
The digitizer is not functioning properly.
The device is in DND mode.
The device has background applications open.
explanation: The device most likely has too many background applications open that are using RAM. That the device is not charged to capacity would not affect RAM. A digitizer not functioning properly would resemble inaccurate touchscreen responses. If the device were in Do Not Disturb (DND) mode, the speakers would not work.
whyWrong: The battery charge level does not change how much RAM the device uses.
A faulty digitizer causes inaccurate touch responses, not low memory.
Do Not Disturb mode silences notifications and calls; it does not use RAM.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 16

stem: What is a risk of using the auto-reconnect feature on a mobile device?
options: The device will reconnect to any SSID.
The device could be exploited by an evil twin attack.
The device's battery life could be shortened.
You may exceed your cellular data plan's limits.
explanation: If auto-reconnect is configured on an SSID, the device could be susceptible to an evil twin attack, in which the device connects to any device with the same SSID. The device will not reconnect to any SSID but only to the SSID configured as auto-reconnect. Battery life will remain unaffected with auto-reconnect. Exceeding limits can be avoided with auto-reconnect, because the wireless network is used for data usage.
whyWrong: Auto-reconnect works only with SSIDs the device has joined before, not with any SSID.
Auto-reconnect does not shorten battery life in any important way.
Auto-reconnect uses Wi-Fi when it is available, which helps avoid going over the cellular data limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 17

stem: What is one consequence of an overheating mobile device?
explanation: Degraded battery life can be expected from an overheating mobile device if the problem persists for a long time. Higher RAM usage will not occur with overheating, but it could be a cause of overheating. Inaccurate touchscreen responses are not a symptom or a consequence of overheating. The inability to decrypt emails depends on having the proper certificate installed.
whyWrong: Higher RAM use can cause overheating, but overheating does not raise RAM use.
Inaccurate touch response comes from a faulty digitizer, not from overheating.
Decrypting email depends on having the right certificate, not on the device temperature.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security, Review Questions question 20

stem: An application won’t close on an Android smartphone. You’ve tried to force stop it—to no avail. What should you do?
options: Stop the underlying service in Running Services.
Take the device to an authorized service center.
explanation: If you’ve already tried to stop the application within Running Services, attempt a soft reset. Hard resets on Android devices should be used only as a last resort because a hard reset will return a device to factory condition—wiping all the data. The question indicates that the application won’t close, not that a service won’t stop, though you could try finding an underlying service that might be the culprit. But you should try resetting the device before doing this or taking it to an authorized service center.
whyWrong: A hard reset wipes all data back to factory condition, so it is a last resort only.
The app will not close, not a service; a soft reset should be tried before hunting for a service.
Taking the phone to a service center is not needed until a soft reset has been tried.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following are valid Wi-Fi troubleshooting methods? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: Make sure the device is within range.
Rename the SSID of the WAP.
explanation: Valid Wi-Fi troubleshooting methods include power cycling the device and making sure the mobile device is within range of the wireless access point. Bluetooth could possibly cause a conflict with Wi-Fi. If you suspect that Bluetooth is interfering, simply turn off Bluetooth. Normally, the mobile device should obtain an IP address dynamically from a DHCP server. Renaming the SSID of the access point could cause problems for all clients trying to connect.
whyWrong: Bluetooth may interfere with Wi-Fi, but the fix is to turn it off, not to restart it.
A mobile device should normally get its IP address from DHCP, so setting a static address is not a fix.
Renaming the SSID of the access point can cause problems for every client that connects to it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: A technician has turned the Portrait Orientation Lock off for an iPhone user. Which common mobile OS problem does this rectify?
options: The Camera app fails to launch.
The battery fails to hold a charge.
explanation: If an iPhone’s or iPad’s screen won’t auto-rotate, the reason is probably that the Portrait Orientation Lock setting is on and locking the display in place. Turning it off unlocks the option, allowing the screen to rotate. In Android, this is simply known as rotation. If the Camera app fails to launch, you might need to restart and/or update the app or restart the phone. If the OS fails to update, you need to troubleshoot the Wi-Fi connection.
whyWrong: A Camera app that fails to launch needs the app or phone restarted or updated, not the orientation lock changed.
An OS that fails to update needs its connection checked; the orientation lock has nothing to do with it.
A battery that does not hold a charge most likely needs service; the orientation lock does not affect it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A user has upgraded to a new mobile device and is preparing to give the old device away. What should the user do before giving it away to ensure that the data is protected?
options: Nothing; the data is already protected.
Perform a soft reset of the device.
Perform a hard reset of the device.
explanation: Perform a hard reset, sometimes called a factory reset. This will erase all data on the device and reset it to factory settings. By doing this, all of the user’s personal information will be erased from the device, and it will be ready for the next user. A soft reset will not only restart the device but will leave all of the data in place.
whyWrong: The data on the old device is not protected until it is erased with a factory reset.
A soft reset only restarts the device and leaves all of the data in place.
Charging the battery does nothing to remove the user's data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 4
note: Factory reset before handing on a device; no exact 220-1202 3.2 topic, mapped to the reset steps under 3.2 (the book's chapter). It also fits 2.9 recycling.

stem: If an application stops responding, which of the following actions can you do to help get back running again?
options: Wait for the application to start working again.
Do a full reset of your mobile device.
explanation: A force stop (force quit in iOS) will quit the application, allowing you to get back to your work right away. While you could wait, a truly locked-up app may never come back (or it may take a long, long time). A full reset of your mobile device is overkill. Although your mobile battery may be part of the problem, and you should always monitor the charge, just having a low battery does not cause an app to lock up.
whyWrong: A truly locked-up app may never recover, or may take a very long time.
A full reset of the device is overkill for one app that stops responding.
A low battery does not make an app lock up, so charging does not fix it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: What can you do to help improve battery life?
options: Ensure that you always charge your battery to 100 percent.
Keep your mobile device on a charger.
explanation: Dimming the screen turns down the backlight, which will use less power. Turning on airplane mode turns off all of the radios in a device (you can turn on individual radios, such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, as needed), so the device draws less power. Keeping your device plugged in is actually counterproductive because keeping the battery topped up shortens battery life.
whyWrong: Always charging to 100 percent does not improve battery life; keeping the battery full shortens it.
Keeping the device on a charger keeps the battery topped up, which shortens battery life.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: One app on a user's Android phone has not updated automatically, although the other apps update normally. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Update the app manually from the Google Play Store
Perform a factory reset of the phone
Roll back the most recent OS update
explanation: App stores normally update installed apps in the background. When one app will not update on its own, the first step is to update it manually from the Play Store or App Store. If that fails, the technician can force-quit the app, reboot, and try again.
whyWrong: A factory reset erases the phone and is far too drastic for one app that will not update.
The other apps update normally, so the OS update is not the cause of this one app's problem.
The battery does not stop one app from updating while the other apps update normally.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

stem: A field technician works all week at sites with no Wi-Fi and uses only cellular data. The apps on his company phone have not updated all week, though automatic updates are turned on. What is the MOST LIKELY reason?
options: The app store treats cellular data as metered and updates apps only over Wi-Fi
The phone's storage is encrypted, which blocks app updates
The apps were removed from the app store by their developers
The phone's screen lock prevents apps from updating
explanation: App stores treat a cellular connection as metered and, by default, install automatic app updates only over Wi-Fi. A user who is on cellular data all week will see no automatic updates. Connecting to Wi-Fi or changing the app store settings to allow cellular updates fixes this.
whyWrong: Device encryption protects data at rest and does not stop the app store from updating apps.
It is very unlikely that every app was removed from the store at the same time.
Apps update in the background while the phone is locked, so the screen lock is not the cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

stem: A user tries to update an app manually from the App Store, but the update still fails. Which TWO troubleshooting steps should the technician try now? (Choose two.)
options: Force-quit the app and reboot the phone
Temporarily disable the antivirus app on the phone and retry the update
Perform a factory reset and restore from a backup
Remove the passcode from the phone
explanation: When a manual update fails, force-quitting the app and rebooting clears any copy of the app stuck in memory. A security app on the device can also block the update, so disabling it for a short time and retrying is the following step. After these steps, the technician tries the manual update again.
whyWrong: A factory reset erases the device and is far too drastic before the simpler steps are tried.
The passcode has no effect on app updates, and removing it only weakens the phone's security.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

stem: A user's seven-year-old tablet will not install the newest major OS version. It is on Wi-Fi, has plenty of free storage, and has been rebooted. What is the MOST LIKELY reason?
options: The tablet's hardware is no longer supported by the new OS version
The tablet's battery is fully charged
The tablet is connected to a metered cellular network
The tablet's screen rotation is locked
explanation: Mobile device makers usually support hardware with OS updates for about 5 to 7 years. After that, newer OS versions are not compatible with the device and will not install. Because connectivity, storage, and a reboot were already checked, compatibility is the remaining cause.
whyWrong: A full battery helps an update install; it is not a reason for an update to fail.
The tablet is on Wi-Fi, so a metered cellular connection is not the cause.
The rotation lock only controls screen orientation and has no effect on OS updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

stem: Sara’s smartphone battery drains quickly even though she does not use it extensively. Which of the following could be a possible cause of the issue?
explanation: Background app refresh is a feature that allows apps to refresh their content in the background, even when they are not actively being used. Enabling this feature for multiple apps can consume significant battery power, causing rapid battery drain.
whyWrong: A dim screen saves battery power, so it cannot explain a battery that drains quickly.
Mobile data use affects the data allowance and does not drain the battery when data is not in use.
Overcharging may wear a battery out over time but does not cause sudden fast drain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 1

stem: David is preparing to use AirDrop to wirelessly share files, photos, and more between Apple devices. Which of the following statements accurately describes AirDrop?
options: AirDrop only works when both devices are connected to the same Wi-Fi network
AirDrop can only be used to transfer files between iPhones
AirDrop requires Bluetooth and Wi-Fi to be enabled on both devices
AirDrop can transfer files between Apple devices and non-Apple devices
explanation: AirDrop requires both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi to be enabled on both devices for the file transfer to take place. Bluetooth is used for device discovery, and Wi-Fi is used for the actual file transfer.
whyWrong: AirDrop makes a direct device-to-device link, so the two devices need not share a Wi-Fi network.
AirDrop also works between iPads and Mac computers, not only between iPhones.
AirDrop works only between Apple devices and cannot send files to other brands.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 2

stem: A user’s smartphone suddenly becomes unresponsive and does not respond to touch inputs. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should be attempted FIRST?
options: Perform a soft reset on the device
Clear the cache of all installed applications
Remove the battery and reinsert it
explanation: Performing a soft reset on the device is the first troubleshooting step to attempt when a smartphone becomes unresponsive. This can be done by holding down the power button until the device restarts. It helps to clear temporary issues or software glitches that may be causing the unresponsiveness.
whyWrong: Clearing every app cache targets app problems, not a device that ignores all touch input.
Reinstalling the mobile OS is a last resort after simpler steps fail.
Most modern phones have sealed batteries, and pulling one is not the first step anyway.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 3

stem: Which of the following technologies enables contactless data exchange between two devices in close proximity?
explanation: Near-field communication (NFC) enables contactless data exchange between two devices in close proximity. It allows devices to establish a connection by bringing them near each other, typically within a few centimeters.
whyWrong: Bluetooth connects devices over several meters and is not the tap-to-share technology.
Wi-Fi covers longer distances and is not designed for contactless exchange at a few centimeters.
GPS receives satellite signals to find a location and does not exchange data between devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 5

stem: A user reports that the screen of their mobile device does not autorotate. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should be performed FIRST to resolve the issue?
explanation: The first troubleshooting step to resolve the issue of the screen not autorotating on a mobile device is to check the screen rotation settings. Sometimes, the autorotate feature may be disabled in the device’s settings, preventing the screen from automatically rotating. By verifying and adjusting the screen rotation settings, the issue can often be resolved without further action.
whyWrong: A restart fixes many problems, but checking whether rotation lock is on is the more direct first step.
An OS update is unlikely to fix rotation that has simply been turned off in settings.
A factory reset erases all data and is a last resort, not a first step.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 6

stem: A user reports that their mobile device randomly reboots while they are using an application. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should be performed FIRST to address this issue?
options: Clear the cache and data of the application
Update the operating system to the latest version
explanation: The most appropriate troubleshooting step to address a mobile device that randomly reboots while using an application is to update the OS to the latest version. This step is crucial as outdated OSs can cause compatibility issues, leading to system instability. Updating the OS ensures that any known bugs or vulnerabilities are addressed, providing a more stable environment for running applications.
whyWrong: Clearing one app's cache and data fixes problems with that app, not reboots of the whole device.
Reinstalling one app helps only when that app alone is the cause of the problem.
A factory reset erases everything and should come only after other steps fail.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 9: Software Troubleshooting, Objective 3.4 question 7

stem: A user reports that their mobile device is running out of storage space and is unable to install new applications. Which of the following actions would be the MOST appropriate troubleshooting step to resolve the issue?
explanation: Uninstalling unnecessary applications will free up storage space on the mobile device and allow the user to install new applications. The storage page in Settings shows how much space each app uses, so the largest unused apps are easy to find and remove.
whyWrong: Clearing the cache frees a little space but does not remove the apps that fill the storage.
A factory reset erases all data and settings, which is far more than this problem needs.
An OS upgrade does not free storage and may even need more space.

stem: A user’s mobile device battery drains quickly, even when not in use. Which of the following actions should be taken to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose two.)
explanation: Closing background applications can help conserve battery power by preventing unnecessary processes from running. Enabling battery optimization settings can also extend battery life.
whyWrong: A new battery is needed only when the battery is old or damaged, and many cannot be replaced.
Push email uses some power but is unlikely to be the main cause of fast battery drain.

stem: A user reports that their mobile device’s touchscreen is unresponsive. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should be performed FIRST to address the issue?
explanation: Restarting the device is the initial troubleshooting step to address various software-related issues, including unresponsive touchscreens. A restart clears temporary software glitches that can stop the screen from responding to touch.
whyWrong: Calibration is a later step to try if the screen still does not respond after a restart.
A firmware update is a later step to try if a restart does not fix the touchscreen.
Cleaning the screen is a later step to try if a restart does not fix the problem.

stem: A mobile device user complains about frequent app crashes. Which of the following actions should be taken to troubleshoot this problem?
explanation: Uninstalling and re-installing the app can resolve app crashes caused by corrupted installation files. Reinstalling replaces the app files with a clean copy from the app store.
whyWrong: Clearing the cache can improve performance but may not fix corrupted installation files.
An OS update is a general step and may not fix the app's own crashes.
A restart is a general step and may not fix the corrupted app files that cause the crashes.

stem: A mobile device user is experiencing slow performance when launching apps and navigating the interface. Which of the following steps should be taken to troubleshoot this problem?
explanation: Clearing app cache and data can help improve performance by removing temporary files and resetting app settings. Large or corrupted cached data can slow apps as they open and run.
whyWrong: A factory reset erases all data and settings and should be avoided unless needed.

explanation: Resetting the device’s network settings can resolve Wi-Fi connectivity issues caused by misconfigured network settings. Forgetting and reconnecting to the Wi-Fi network is a less drastic step and can also help establish a stable connection.

explanation: Deleting unnecessary files and applications will free up storage space on the device and resolve the Insufficient storage available issue. Removing files and apps that are no longer needed is the quickest way to get usable space back.

stem: A sales rep on a week-long trip says her company phone has shown a pending OS update for days. The phone has plenty of free storage, and she has used only cellular data during the trip. What is the MOST LIKELY reason the update has not installed?
options: The phone will not download large OS updates over a metered cellular connection
The phone's battery is too old to accept an update
The phone's orientation sensor has failed
The app store has automatic app updates turned off
explanation: Many mobile operating systems treat cellular data as a metered connection and wait for Wi-Fi before they download a large update. Connecting to a stable Wi-Fi network lets the update download and install.
whyWrong: An old battery shortens battery life, but it does not stop an update from downloading.
A failed orientation sensor stops the screen from rotating; it has nothing to do with updates.

stem: A warehouse worker says his phone's battery runs out by noon, but only on days he works in the basement stock room, where the phone usually shows no signal bars. No app shows unusual battery use. What is the BEST advice for the technician to give?
options: Turn on Airplane mode in the stock room and turn on Wi-Fi only if it is needed
Perform a factory reset of the phone
Turn off the orientation lock in quick settings
Clear the cache of every installed app
explanation: In a dead spot a phone keeps searching for a cellular signal, and that search drains the battery. Airplane mode turns off all the radios, and the user can turn Wi-Fi back on alone. This saves power without losing the data on the phone.
whyWrong: A factory reset erases all data and does not stop the phone from searching for a signal.
The orientation lock only controls screen rotation and has no effect on battery drain.
Clearing app caches can fix app problems, but no app shows high battery use here.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

stem: A nurse says the scheduling app on her clinic tablet now closes as soon as she opens it. The problem began right after the app updated itself last night, and other apps work normally. Which of the following should the technician do FIRST?
options: Force stop the app and restart the tablet
Perform a factory reset of the tablet
Install the app from a file on the vendor's website
explanation: A force stop and a restart are quick, safe first steps that clear an app stuck in memory. If the app still fails, clearing its cache or reinstalling it comes next. A factory reset is a last resort because it erases the device.

stem: Which of the following could result from downloading something from an untrusted source? (Select all that apply.)

stem: You suspect that a mobile device has been compromised and is now part of a botnet. What are some of the indicators that this has happened? (Select the two BEST answers.)

Take the device off the network, isolate it, and run a scan of the device; you are on the hunt for Trojans especially.
